title: The first public dates: the heavyweight six on a Connecticut bus, then Virginia
summary: The first one-nighters were in Connecticut, where the big men stepping off the bus looked like football players, followed by Norfolk and Richmond, and much later the Deep South.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Okay. Well let's go back to how the group developed as an actual performing group, rather than just as a recording group. When -- where did you start? Do you remember when, or at least where the first -- you first played together in public, rather than in a recording studio?
Other than at a recording studio, huh?
Well, I'm trying to think now --
(Telephone interruption.)
Okay, the phone just rang, and now we're off the phone. We were talking about when the Fats Waller group first started playing before the public.
Well, I think -- well I know we did a few things up in Connecticut, and all that. I heard --
Those were one-nighters.

Yeah, well I have a -- I've got to tell this. We went up to -- uh, not to far up into Connecticut. By golly, what's the name of the damn town? Anyway, we went up there, so when the bus -- we had a bus. It took the small group, the six guys -- (laughs) -- we stopped right in front of the joint. A lot of guys run out to see, oh here's the band.

And now -- I've got to name these guys. Charlie Turner is bass player. He weighed 290 pounds, at least, you know. And that's a pretty good sized man. At that time Fats was weighing 285, 90, maybe three, you know. At that time Herman Autrey was weighing about 245 or 50. Emmett Matthews was weighing about the same. And we had a drummer with us who is now -- he's working in the parks. He works for the Park Service. The thing here in New York? Uh -- uh, uh, uh, he's six foot three or four. He was weighing 200 and something, and who else was on -- who else was there? He's the
drummer.
[You had the]
: (Inaudible) drummer?
Yeah, piano I'm trying to think.
That's about everybody, isn't it?
That's about six of them?
I think so.
And when we stepped out of the bus, man, the guy said, Jesus what a band! Got football players, or what.
(Laughter.)
All of the big guys, and there was some -- naturally we were some pretty grown up men.

Now after we did the date up there, we sounded pretty good, but after that we went to Virginia, we started working down in Norfolk, Richmond, Virginia, a few things around there, I'm trying to think -- now I'm trying to think, we -- did we go into the Carolinas then? I don't think -- I'm not positive.

And back in New York, we did go to the Carolinas, and on down, we went down, on further down, we hit Georgia, and Alabama, and all that stuff, much later, you know. Doing one-nighters. But that's the way it -- that's the way it started, you know?
